chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Al-Husayn ibn Usman, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who gives the zakat of his wealth to a man and he considers him to be financially straitened, but he finds him to be affluent, he said: It is not sufficient for him.
ai.seo_question: What happens to the validity of zakat if the recipient turns out to be wealthy instead of poor?
ai.summary: This ruling from al-Kafi underscores the principle of 'good faith' in zakat distribution, where the giver's sincere belief in the recipient's poverty at the time of payment is sufficient for validity, even if later proven incorrect. It reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on the giver's intention and the practical ease of distribution, distinguishing it from stricter conditions found in some Sunni schools. The hadith serves as a practical guideline for believers to avoid excessive scrutiny that might hinder the timely fulfillment of this obligatory charity.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Al Husayn Bin Usman, from the one who mentioned it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>

regarding a man who gave the Zakāt of his wealth to a man and he saw him as financially straitened, but he found him to be affluent (after paying him)’. Heasws said: ‘He would not be sufficed from it (i.e. he has to pay again)’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu ‘Umayr from al-Husayn ibn ‘Uthman from the one whom he has mentioned who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who pays Zakat to a person whom as he sees is a needy person, but later finds out to be affluent. He (the Imam) said, ‘Such payment is not sufficient for Zakat.’”
